section_summary: This section contains diplomatic notes, departmental memoranda, and inter-agency letters between the Japanese Embassy, the U.S. Department of State, and the Treasury Department from December 1939 to June 1940. The predominant issue is the Japanese Embassy's request for income tax exemption for Japanese naval officers assigned to Los Angeles to supervise extensive crude oil and fuel purchases, which the State Department and Navy Department strongly oppose as an improper extension of foreign governmental offices beyond normal diplomatic channels, eventually forcing Japan to reassign the officers to New York. The remainder of the correspondence concerns statutory reciprocal income tax exemptions under Section 116(h) of the Internal Revenue Code and biographical filings for Japanese military inspectors, government railway and financial officials, academic researchers, and staff representing Japan at the 1939–1940 New York World's Fair and the Golden Gate International Exposition in San Francisco.

subfiles.about: The Japanese Embassy requests federal income tax exemptions for three Japanese naval officials stationed in Los Angeles.
subfiles.summary: The Japanese Ambassador presents compliments to the Secretary of State and requests income tax exemption for Commander Arito Yatugi, Commander Tokiji Taira, and Mr. Goro Isimaru. They were dispatched by the Japanese Government as officials of the Imperial Japanese Navy Inspector's Office in New York City but assigned to duty in Los Angeles, residing at the Miyako Hotel. The Ambassador asks that their names be brought to the attention of appropriate United States authorities.
subfiles.title: Japanese Embassy Note No. 295 regarding Tax Exemption for Naval Officials in Los Angeles

subfiles.about: The Division of Far Eastern Affairs advises against allowing Japan to establish a naval inspectorate suboffice in Los Angeles.
subfiles.summary: Cabot Coville of the Division of Far Eastern Affairs notes that it is considered undesirable to allow the Japanese Government to establish a suboffice of its New York Naval Inspectorate in Los Angeles. FE redrafted the proposed reply to Japanese Embassy note 295 concerning Commander Yatugi, Commander Taira, and Mr. Isimaru. It suggests withholding the certification letter to the Treasury Department until Japan indicates reassignment of the naval personnel.
subfiles.title: State Department Memorandum on Japanese Naval Inspectorate Suboffice in Los Angeles

subfiles.about: The Secretary of State informs the Japanese Ambassador that the United States does not favor establishing a Japanese naval inspectorate office in Los Angeles.
subfiles.summary: The Secretary of State acknowledges receipt of Japanese Embassy note no. 295 concerning the income tax exemption of Commander Arito Yatugi, Commander Tokiji Taira, and Mr. Goro Isimaru. He notes the statement that these officials were sent by the Japanese Government as part of the Imperial Japanese Navy Inspector's Office at New York and assigned to Los Angeles. The Secretary officially informs the Ambassador that the American Government does not view with favor the extension of the activities of the Japanese Naval Inspector's Office by assigning personnel to Los Angeles.
subfiles.title: State Department Note to Japanese Ambassador declining Naval Inspectorate Extension to Los Angeles

subfiles.about: A drafted certification letter from the State Department to the Treasury Department regarding tax exemption for three Japanese naval officials.
subfiles.summary: The Secretary of State transmits to Treasury Secretary Henry Morgenthau, Jr. a copy of the Japanese Ambassador's note requesting Federal income tax exemption for Commander Arito Yatugi, Commander Tokiji Taira, and Mr. Goro Isimaru. In accordance with Section 116(h) of the Internal Revenue Code, the Department provides reciprocal certification that Japan grants equivalent exemptions to U.S. government employees. The letter was held unissued pursuant to Far Eastern Affairs policy.
subfiles.title: Draft State Department Letter to Secretary of the Treasury regarding Tax Exemption for Yatugi, Taira, and Isimaru
subfiles.to: Henry Morgenthau, Jr., Secretary of the Treasury

subfiles.about: A draft State Department note acknowledging receipt of the Japanese Embassy's tax exemption request.
subfiles.summary: The draft note acknowledges the Japanese Ambassador's note no. 295 of December 14, 1939 regarding tax exemption for Commander Yatugi, Commander Taira, and Mr. Isimaru. It drafts a standard notification stating that a copy has been forwarded to the competent authority of the United States Government. This draft was subsequently revised to express disapproval of the Los Angeles office.
subfiles.title: Draft State Department Note to Japanese Ambassador acknowledging Note No. 295

subfiles.about: The Treasury Department confirms tax exemption instructions for Commanders Murata and Watari.
subfiles.summary: The Acting Secretary of the Treasury acknowledges the State Department's letter of December 28, 1939 certifying reciprocal tax exemption for Commander Tosio Murata and Commander Katumi Watari of the Imperial Japanese Navy Inspector's Office in New York. Pursuant to Section 116(h) of the Internal Revenue Code and the State Department's certification, instructions will be issued to Internal Revenue officials.
subfiles.title: Treasury Department Letter regarding Tax Exemption for Commander Murata and Commander Watari

subfiles.about: The Treasury Department confirms tax exemption instructions for Japanese World's Fair and Exposition officials.
subfiles.summary: The Acting Secretary of the Treasury acknowledges the Secretary of State's letter of January 3, 1940 concerning tax exemption for Japanese officials representing the Japanese Association for the New York World's Fair and the Golden Gate International Exposition. It is noted that the named officials will sail from San Francisco on January 18th. Appropriate tax exemption instructions will be issued to Internal Revenue officials under Section 116(h).
subfiles.title: Treasury Department Letter regarding Tax Exemption for Japanese Exposition Officials

subfiles.about: The Treasury Department confirms tax exemption instructions for Commander Ryoichi Shiraishi.
subfiles.summary: The Acting Secretary of the Treasury acknowledges the State Department's letter of January 4, 1940 concerning income tax exemption for Commander Ryoichi Shiraishi, Accounting Inspector of the Naval Technical Department and Department of Naval Aeronautics. Shiraishi is scheduled to sail from San Francisco on January 18. Treasury confirms that appropriate instructions will be issued to Internal Revenue officials under Section 116(h).
subfiles.title: Treasury Department Letter regarding Tax Exemption for Commander Ryoichi Shiraishi

subfiles.about: The Treasury Department confirms tax exemption instructions for Lieutenant Commander Kanegoro Koike.
subfiles.summary: The Acting Secretary of the Treasury acknowledges the State Department's certification of January 13, 1940 regarding Lieutenant Commander Kanegoro Koike, Accounting Inspector of the Naval Technical Department and Department of Naval Aeronautics. Pursuant to Section 116(h) of the Internal Revenue Code, appropriate instructions will be issued to Internal Revenue officials.
subfiles.title: Treasury Department Letter regarding Tax Exemption for Lieutenant Commander Kanegoro Koike

subfiles.about: The Japanese Embassy reports the scheduled departure of Yoshisuke Isoda, Secretary to the Financial Commission.
subfiles.summary: The Japanese Ambassador informs the Secretary of State that Mr. Yoshisuke Isoda, Secretary to the Financial Commission of the Imperial Japanese Government in New York City, will depart from the United States. Isoda is scheduled to leave San Francisco on March 14, 1940 aboard the steamship Asama Maru. The Ambassador requests that this departure be communicated to the appropriate authorities regarding his tax exemption.
subfiles.title: Japanese Embassy Note No. 35 regarding Departure of Yoshisuke Isoda

subfiles.about: The State Department notifies the Treasury Department of the departure and tax-exempt status of Yoshisuke Isoda.
subfiles.from: Breckinridge Long, Assistant Secretary of State
subfiles.summary: Assistant Secretary of State Breckinridge Long transmits to Treasury Secretary Henry Morgenthau, Jr. a copy of Japanese Embassy note no. 35 regarding Mr. Yoshisuke Isoda. Reference is made to the previous certification under Section 116(h) of the Internal Revenue Code on April 29, 1939. The Treasury is notified of Isoda's planned departure from San Francisco on March 14 on the steamship Asama Maru.
subfiles.title: State Department Letter to Secretary of the Treasury regarding Yoshisuke Isoda
subfiles.to: Henry Morgenthau, Jr., Secretary of the Treasury

subfiles.about: The State Department acknowledges the Japanese Embassy's notification regarding the departure of Yoshisuke Isoda.
subfiles.summary: The Secretary of State acknowledges receipt of Japanese Embassy note no. 35 concerning the desired income tax exemption and departure of Yoshisuke Isoda, Secretary to the Financial Commission. The Ambassador is informed that the details have been forwarded to the competent authority of the United States Government.
subfiles.title: State Department Note to Japanese Ambassador acknowledging Note No. 35

subfiles.about: The Japanese Embassy requests tax exemption for Lieutenant Commander Yuzuru Sanematu, language officer in New York.
subfiles.summary: The Japanese Ambassador requests that Lieutenant Commander Yuzuru Sanematu be granted income tax exemption. Sanematu was sent to the United States as a Language Officer attached to the Japanese Naval Inspector's Office in New York City, arriving in San Francisco on February 9, 1940 aboard the steamship Kamakura Maru. The Ambassador asks that his name be brought to the attention of appropriate United States authorities.
subfiles.title: Japanese Embassy Note No. 45 requesting Tax Exemption for Lieutenant Commander Yuzuru Sanematu

subfiles.about: The State Department transmits a Section 116(h) tax exemption certification for Lieutenant Commander Sanematu to the Treasury.
subfiles.summary: Secretary of State Cordell Hull transmits to Treasury Secretary Henry Morgenthau, Jr. a copy of Japanese Embassy note no. 45 regarding Lieutenant Commander Yuzuru Sanematu. Hull certifies under Section 116(h) of the Internal Revenue Code that Japan grants equivalent exemptions to U.S. government employees performing services in Japan.
subfiles.title: State Department Letter to Secretary of the Treasury regarding Lieutenant Commander Sanematu
subfiles.to: Henry Morgenthau, Jr., Secretary of the Treasury

subfiles.about: The State Department informs the Japanese Ambassador that Lieutenant Commander Sanematu's tax exemption request has been forwarded.
subfiles.summary: The Secretary of State acknowledges receipt of Japanese Embassy note no. 45 regarding Lieutenant Commander Yuzuru Sanematu. The Ambassador is informed that the note has been transmitted to the competent authority of the United States Government with a view to exempting Sanematu from Federal income tax.
subfiles.title: State Department Note to Japanese Ambassador acknowledging Note No. 45

subfiles.about: The State Department requests biographical data on Sanematu and inquires what action Japan is taking regarding naval personnel in Los Angeles.
subfiles.summary: The Secretary of State requests further information regarding Lieutenant Commander Yuzuru Sanematu on an enclosed standard form. The note further references an Embassy note of February 28 transmitting naval employee records that included Commander Yatugi, Commander Taira, and Mr. Isimaru, who were assigned to Los Angeles. Reminding the Ambassador that the U.S. does not favor extending the Naval Inspector's Office to Los Angeles, the Secretary requests to be informed what steps Japan is taking in pursuance of this view.
subfiles.title: State Department Note to Japanese Ambassador requesting Biographical Form and Action on Los Angeles Personnel

subfiles.about: The Treasury Department confirms tax exemption instructions for Lieutenant Commander Yuzuru Sanematu.
subfiles.summary: The Acting Secretary of the Treasury acknowledges the State Department's letter of February 28, 1940 regarding Lieutenant Commander Yuzuru Sanematu. In view of the State Department's certification under Section 116(h) of the Internal Revenue Code, appropriate instructions will be issued to Internal Revenue officials.
subfiles.title: Treasury Department Letter regarding Tax Exemption for Lieutenant Commander Sanematu

subfiles.about: A cross-reference sheet regarding biographical records transmitted for Yoshio Sudo and Surgeon Lieutenant-Colonel Masataka Kitagawa.
subfiles.summary: A cross-reference sheet indexing a Japanese Embassy communication dated February 29, 1940 (file 702.9411b/25). The communication transmitted biographical records for Yoshio Sudo, an officer of the Japan Tourist Bureau at Manila, and Surgeon Lieutenant-Colonel Masataka Kitagawa, a student of tropical diseases at the University of the Philippines in Manila.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Sheet regarding Biographical Records of Yoshio Sudo and Masataka Kitagawa

subfiles.about: The Japanese Embassy transmits biographical records for Lieutenant Oyama and Military Engineer Yukiyoshi Suto.
subfiles.summary: The Japanese Ambassador transmits biographical records for Lieutenant Oyama and Military Engineer Yukiyoshi Suto. Both are identified as members of the staff of the Japanese Military Inspector's Office in New York City.
subfiles.title: Japanese Embassy Note transmitting Biographical Records of Lieutenant Oyama and Yukiyoshi Suto

subfiles.about: A memorandum of conversation between Counselor Morishima and Maxwell M. Hamilton concerning the proposed Los Angeles naval office.
subfiles.summary: Japanese Embassy Counselor Morito Morishima explains that State's note of January 8 had initially been routed to subordinate staff due to its tax wording, but that Japan wished to ask if the U.S. could reconsider its decision opposing naval personnel in Los Angeles. Morishima emphasizes that personnel were needed to facilitate oil purchases. Hamilton replies that U.S. policy restricts expanding foreign governmental offices outside regular diplomatic missions, that the decision was firm, and that Japan could continue its past practice of sending officers on temporary trips from New York without establishing an office.
subfiles.title: Memorandum of Conversation between Morito Morishima and Maxwell M. Hamilton regarding Los Angeles Naval Office

subfiles.about: Maxwell M. Hamilton transmits memoranda of conversations regarding the Japanese Naval Inspectorate to the Navy Department.
subfiles.summary: Maxwell M. Hamilton transmits two memoranda of conversations dated March 15 and 27, 1940 with Japanese Embassy Counselor Morishima to Captain Roscoe E. Schuirmann, Director of the Central Division of the Navy Department. Hamilton notes that he expects to telephone Schuirmann after the Captain has reviewed the memoranda regarding the extension of the Japanese Naval Inspector's Office to Los Angeles.
subfiles.title: Memorandum from Maxwell M. Hamilton to Captain Roscoe E. Schuirmann
subfiles.to: Captain Roscoe E. Schuirmann, Navy Department

subfiles.about: The Japanese Embassy requests income tax exemption for Professor Minoru Takada of Keijo Imperial University.
subfiles.summary: The Japanese Ambassador requests income tax exemption for Mr. Minoru Takada, Professor of Keijo Imperial University, who was sent to the United States to study applied electrical engineering. Takada is residing at the Yamato Hotel in New York City, having arrived in San Francisco on March 21, 1940 aboard the steamship Tatuta Maru. His income is derived solely from the Japanese Government.
subfiles.title: Japanese Embassy Note No. 77 requesting Tax Exemption for Minoru Takada

subfiles.about: The State Department transmits a Section 116(h) tax exemption certification for Professor Minoru Takada to the Treasury.
subfiles.summary: Secretary of State Cordell Hull transmits a copy of Japanese Embassy note no. 77 concerning Mr. Minoru Takada to Treasury Secretary Henry Morgenthau, Jr. Under Section 116(h) of the Internal Revenue Code, Hull certifies that Japan grants equivalent tax exemptions to American officials and that Takada's official compensation qualifies for reciprocal exemption.
subfiles.title: State Department Letter to Secretary of the Treasury regarding Minoru Takada
subfiles.to: Henry Morgenthau, Jr., Secretary of the Treasury

subfiles.about: The State Department acknowledges the Japanese Embassy's tax exemption request for Professor Minoru Takada.
subfiles.summary: The Secretary of State acknowledges receipt of Japanese Embassy note no. 77 concerning Professor Minoru Takada. The Ambassador is informed that a copy has been transmitted to the competent authority of the United States Government with a view to granting the requested Federal income tax exemption.
subfiles.title: State Department Note to Japanese Ambassador acknowledging Note No. 77

subfiles.about: The Japanese Embassy requests income tax exemption for Hirotaka Tsuda of the Japanese Government Railways.
subfiles.summary: The Japanese Ambassador requests income tax exemption for Mr. Hirotaka Tsuda, who was sent to the United States as Secretary to the Japanese Government Railways at 630 Fifth Avenue, New York City. Tsuda arrived in New York on February 21, 1940 on the steamship Vulcania, and his income is derived solely from the Japanese Government.
subfiles.title: Japanese Embassy Note No. 78 requesting Tax Exemption for Hirotaka Tsuda

subfiles.about: The State Department transmits a Section 116(h) tax exemption certification for Hirotaka Tsuda to the Treasury.
subfiles.summary: Secretary of State Cordell Hull transmits Japanese Embassy note no. 78 concerning Mr. Hirotaka Tsuda to Treasury Secretary Henry Morgenthau, Jr. Hull certifies that the Japanese Government grants an equivalent income tax exemption to U.S. government employees in Japan pursuant to Section 116(h) of the Internal Revenue Code.
subfiles.title: State Department Letter to Secretary of the Treasury regarding Hirotaka Tsuda
subfiles.to: Henry Morgenthau, Jr., Secretary of the Treasury

subfiles.about: The State Department acknowledges the Japanese Embassy's request regarding Hirotaka Tsuda.
subfiles.summary: The Secretary of State acknowledges receipt of Japanese Embassy note no. 78 regarding Mr. Hirotaka Tsuda of the Japanese Government Railways. The Ambassador is informed that the note has been transmitted to the competent authority of the United States Government.
subfiles.title: State Department Note to Japanese Ambassador acknowledging Note No. 78

subfiles.about: The Japanese Embassy informs the State Department of the upcoming departure of Assistant Professor Yoshiyuki Inouye.
subfiles.summary: The Japanese Ambassador notifies the Secretary of State of the scheduled departure of Mr. Yoshiyuki Inouye, Assistant Professor of Kyoto Imperial University, who served as a language officer at the Takamine Laboratory in Clifton, New Jersey. Inouye is scheduled to leave New York on May 3, 1940 aboard the steamship Santa Lucia. The Ambassador requests that this departure be reported to the appropriate authorities.
subfiles.title: Japanese Embassy Note No. 79 regarding Departure of Yoshiyuki Inouye

subfiles.about: The State Department notifies the Treasury Department of the departure and tax status of Yoshiyuki Inouye.
subfiles.summary: Secretary of State Cordell Hull transmits to Treasury Secretary Henry Morgenthau, Jr. a copy of Japanese Embassy note no. 79 regarding Mr. Yoshiyuki Inouye. Hull certifies reciprocal exemption under Section 116(h) of the Internal Revenue Code and informs the Treasury of Inouye's upcoming departure from New York on May 3 aboard the steamship Santa Lucia.
subfiles.title: State Department Letter to Secretary of the Treasury regarding Yoshiyuki Inouye
subfiles.to: Henry Morgenthau, Jr., Secretary of the Treasury

subfiles.about: The State Department acknowledges the Japanese Embassy's note regarding the departure of Yoshiyuki Inouye.
subfiles.summary: The Secretary of State acknowledges receipt of Japanese Embassy note no. 79 regarding Mr. Yoshiyuki Inouye. The Ambassador is informed that the note has been forwarded to the competent authority of the United States Government.
subfiles.title: State Department Note to Japanese Ambassador acknowledging Note No. 79

subfiles.about: Maxwell M. Hamilton reports informing Counselor Morishima that the U.S. decision against stationing naval personnel in Los Angeles remains unchanged.
subfiles.summary: Maxwell M. Hamilton records meeting with Counselor Morito Morishima of the Japanese Embassy. Hamilton informed Morishima that appropriate U.S. officers had reconsidered the question of extending the Japanese Naval Inspector's Office to Los Angeles in light of Japan's informal representations, but decided that the United States could not alter its previous negative decision. Hamilton reiterated the administrative policy reasons previously explained.
subfiles.title: State Department Memorandum on Meeting with Morito Morishima regarding Los Angeles Personnel

subfiles.about: Maxwell M. Hamilton recommends standing pat against Japanese naval personnel in Los Angeles, which Under Secretary Welles approves.
subfiles.summary: Maxwell M. Hamilton writes to Under Secretary Sumner Welles regarding Japan's repeated informal requests to reconsider stationing naval personnel in Los Angeles. Hamilton notes that Captain Schuirmann of the Navy Department advised that the U.S. should stand pat, an opinion shared by Stanley K. Hornbeck and the Division of Far Eastern Affairs. Hamilton requests authorization to inform Counselor Morishima that the decision will not be altered, which Welles formally approves.
subfiles.title: State Department Memorandum for Under Secretary Welles regarding Japanese Naval Personnel in Los Angeles
subfiles.to: Sumner Welles, Under Secretary of State

subfiles.about: A detailed memorandum of conversation between Counselor Morishima and Maxwell M. Hamilton detailing Japanese oil purchases in Los Angeles.
subfiles.summary: Counselor Morito Morishima meets with Maxwell M. Hamilton to provide detailed operational justifications for stationing naval personnel in Los Angeles, including one accounting officer, one engineering officer, and one clerk. Morishima reveals that Japan purchases $10,000,000 worth of oil annually from the Los Angeles region, that 32 oil tankers sailed in the first quarter of 1940 alone, and that the Diet had specifically appropriated funds for the Los Angeles post. Hamilton responds that basic facts were already known and that the U.S. position was unlikely to change, but promises to consult colleagues again.
subfiles.title: Memorandum of Conversation between Morito Morishima and Maxwell M. Hamilton on Japanese Oil Purchases

subfiles.about: The Treasury Department confirms tax exemption instructions for Professor Minoru Takada.
subfiles.summary: The Acting Secretary of the Treasury acknowledges the State Department's letter of April 18, 1940 certifying reciprocal exemption for Mr. Minoru Takada. Pursuant to Section 116(h) of the Internal Revenue Code, appropriate instructions will be issued to Internal Revenue officials.
subfiles.title: Treasury Department Letter regarding Tax Exemption for Minoru Takada

subfiles.about: The Treasury Department confirms tax exemption instructions for Hirotaka Tsuda.
subfiles.summary: The Acting Secretary of the Treasury acknowledges the State Department's letter of April 18, 1940 concerning Mr. Hirotaka Tsuda of the Japanese Government Railways. In view of the State Department's certification under Section 116(h) of the Internal Revenue Code, appropriate instructions will be issued to Internal Revenue officials.
subfiles.title: Treasury Department Letter regarding Tax Exemption for Hirotaka Tsuda

subfiles.about: The Treasury Department confirms tax exemption instructions for Yoshiyuki Inouye.
subfiles.summary: The Acting Secretary of the Treasury acknowledges the State Department's letter of April 17, 1940 regarding Mr. Yoshiyuki Inouye, who is scheduled to depart on May 3. Appropriate instructions will be issued to Internal Revenue officials under Section 116(h) of the Internal Revenue Code.
subfiles.title: Treasury Department Letter regarding Tax Exemption for Yoshiyuki Inouye

subfiles.about: Joseph W. Ballantine suggests correcting State Department records pursuant to the Japanese Embassy's note on naval personnel.
subfiles.summary: Joseph W. Ballantine of the Division of Far Eastern Affairs advises the Division of Personnel (DP) to update departmental records in accordance with the attached Japanese Embassy note of April 23, 1940 regarding the return of naval officials from Los Angeles.
subfiles.title: State Department Memorandum regarding Record Corrections for Japanese Naval Personnel

subfiles.about: Maxwell M. Hamilton records Counselor Morishima's delivery of Note No. 87 and his comment on naval officers' locations.
subfiles.summary: Maxwell M. Hamilton notes that Counselor Morito Morishima called on April 23 and delivered Japanese Embassy note no. 87. Morishima explained that the naval officers mentioned in the note had remained in Washington for the past month.
subfiles.title: State Department Memorandum on Delivery of Japanese Embassy Note No. 87

subfiles.about: The Japanese Embassy informs the State Department that the three naval officials in Los Angeles have been ordered to return to New York.
subfiles.summary: The Japanese Ambassador informs the Secretary of State that Commander Arito Yatugi, Commander Tokoji Taira, and Mr. Goro Isimaru have received orders to return to duty at the Imperial Japanese Navy Inspector's Office in New York City, ending their Los Angeles assignment. The Ambassador adds that because officials must supervise naval fuel purchases, they intend to make temporary visits to Los Angeles as circumstances require.
subfiles.title: Japanese Embassy Note No. 87 regarding Reassignment of Naval Personnel to New York

subfiles.about: The State Department certifies reciprocal tax exemption to the Treasury for Yatugi, Taira, and Isimaru following their reassignment to New York.
subfiles.from: Sumner Welles, Acting Secretary of State
subfiles.summary: Acting Secretary of State Sumner Welles writes to Treasury Secretary Henry Morgenthau, Jr. requesting Federal income tax exemption for Commander Arito Yatugi, Commander Tokoji Taira, and Mr. Goro Isimaru. Having received confirmation of their reassignment to the Imperial Japanese Navy Inspector's Office in New York City, Welles issues the official reciprocal exemption certification under Section 116(h) of the Internal Revenue Code.
subfiles.title: State Department Letter to Secretary of the Treasury granting Tax Exemption for Yatugi, Taira, and Isimaru
subfiles.to: Henry Morgenthau, Jr., Secretary of the Treasury

subfiles.about: The State Department acknowledges receipt of Note No. 87 and notes the transfer of naval personnel to New York for tax exemption purposes.
subfiles.summary: The Secretary of State acknowledges Japanese Embassy note no. 87 of April 23, 1940 reporting that Commander Yatugi, Commander Taira, and Mr. Isimaru have received orders returning them to New York. The Ambassador is informed that the competent U.S. authority has been notified of their assignment to the New York office with a view to their Federal income tax exemption.
subfiles.title: State Department Note to Japanese Ambassador acknowledging Note No. 87

subfiles.about: The Treasury Department confirms tax exemption instructions for Commander Yatugi, Commander Taira, and Mr. Isimaru in New York.
subfiles.summary: The Acting Secretary of the Treasury acknowledges the State Department's letter of May 3, 1940 certifying the tax-exempt status of Commander Arito Yatugi, Commander Tokoji Taira, and Mr. Goro Isimaru at the Imperial Japanese Navy Inspector's Office in New York. Pursuant to Section 116(h) of the Internal Revenue Code, appropriate instructions will be issued to Internal Revenue officials.
subfiles.title: Treasury Department Letter regarding Tax Exemption for Yatugi, Taira, and Isimaru

subfiles.about: A certified file copy of the second page of the State Department's note to the Japanese Ambassador of May 8, 1940.
subfiles.summary: A duplicate file copy of the concluding page of the State Department's note of May 8, 1940 to the Japanese Ambassador. It confirms that competent authorities have been notified regarding the tax exemption of Commander Yatugi, Commander Taira, and Mr. Isimaru upon their return to New York.
subfiles.title: State Department Note to Japanese Ambassador (Duplicate Concluding Page)

subfiles.about: A duplicate file copy of the Treasury Department's letter confirming tax exemption instructions for Yatugi, Taira, and Isimaru.
subfiles.summary: A duplicate carbon copy of the letter from Acting Secretary of the Treasury John L. Sullivan to the Secretary of State dated May 9, 1940. It confirms that instructions will be issued to Internal Revenue officials granting tax exemptions under Section 116(h) for Commander Yatugi, Commander Taira, and Mr. Isimaru.
subfiles.title: Treasury Department Letter regarding Tax Exemption for Yatugi, Taira, and Isimaru (Duplicate Copy)

subfiles.about: The Japanese Embassy reports the scheduled departure of naval inspector Moritoshi Maeda.
subfiles.summary: The Japanese Ambassador informs the Secretary of State of the departure of Mr. Moritoshi Maeda, Engineer and Inspector of Construction and Ordnance of the Naval Technical Department at the Japanese Naval Inspector's Office in New York. Maeda is scheduled to depart San Francisco on May 25, 1940 aboard the steamship Tatsuta Maru. The Ambassador requests that this departure be reported to the appropriate authorities.
subfiles.title: Japanese Embassy Note No. 104 regarding Departure of Moritoshi Maeda

subfiles.about: An initial draft/file copy of the State Department's Section 116(h) certification letter for Moritoshi Maeda.
subfiles.summary: An initial file copy of page 1 of the State Department's letter to Treasury Secretary Henry Morgenthau, Jr. concerning Mr. Moritoshi Maeda. It transmits Japanese Embassy note no. 104 and begins the statutory certification under Section 116(h) of the Internal Revenue Code.
subfiles.title: State Department Draft Letter to Secretary of the Treasury regarding Moritoshi Maeda
subfiles.to: Henry Morgenthau, Jr., Secretary of the Treasury

subfiles.about: The State Department certifies the tax-exempt status of naval inspector Moritoshi Maeda to the Treasury.
subfiles.summary: Secretary of State Cordell Hull transmits Japanese Embassy note no. 104 regarding Mr. Moritoshi Maeda to Treasury Secretary Henry Morgenthau, Jr. Hull certifies under Section 116(h) of the Internal Revenue Code that Japan grants equivalent exemptions to U.S. government employees performing services in Japan and that Maeda qualifies for reciprocal exemption.
subfiles.title: State Department Letter to Secretary of the Treasury regarding Moritoshi Maeda
subfiles.to: Henry Morgenthau, Jr., Secretary of the Treasury

subfiles.about: The State Department acknowledges the Japanese Embassy's notification regarding Moritoshi Maeda.
subfiles.summary: The Secretary of State acknowledges receipt of Japanese Embassy note no. 104 regarding Mr. Moritoshi Maeda. The Ambassador is informed that the note has been forwarded to the competent authority of the United States Government.
subfiles.title: State Department Note to Japanese Ambassador acknowledging Note No. 104

subfiles.about: The Japanese Embassy requests income tax exemption for Kiyoshi Murai of the Raw Silk Conditioning House.
subfiles.summary: The Japanese Ambassador requests income tax exemption for Mr. Kiyoshi Murai, technical expert of the Japanese Government Raw Silk Conditioning House at 261 Fifth Avenue, New York City. Murai arrived in San Francisco on December 14, 1939 aboard the steamship Kamakura Maru, with income derived solely from the Japanese Government.
subfiles.title: Japanese Embassy Note No. 106 requesting Tax Exemption for Kiyoshi Murai

subfiles.about: The State Department certifies the tax-exempt status of Kiyoshi Murai to the Treasury.
subfiles.summary: Secretary of State Cordell Hull transmits Japanese Embassy note no. 106 regarding Mr. Kiyoshi Murai to Treasury Secretary Henry Morgenthau, Jr. Hull provides reciprocal certification under Section 116(h) of the Internal Revenue Code that Japan grants equivalent tax exemptions to American officials in Japan.
subfiles.title: State Department Letter to Secretary of the Treasury regarding Kiyoshi Murai
subfiles.to: Henry Morgenthau, Jr., Secretary of the Treasury

subfiles.about: The State Department acknowledges the Japanese Embassy's request regarding Kiyoshi Murai.
subfiles.summary: The Secretary of State acknowledges receipt of Japanese Embassy note no. 106 regarding Mr. Kiyoshi Murai of the Japanese Government Raw Silk Conditioning House. The Ambassador is informed that the note has been transmitted to the competent authority of the United States Government.
subfiles.title: State Department Note to Japanese Ambassador acknowledging Note No. 106

subfiles.about: The State Department requests standard biographical information regarding Kiyoshi Murai.
subfiles.summary: The Secretary of State references the Department's note of May 21 regarding Kiyoshi Murai's tax exemption and requests that the Japanese Embassy furnish detailed biographical information concerning Mr. Murai on an enclosed standard form.
subfiles.title: State Department Note to Japanese Ambassador requesting Biographical Form for Kiyoshi Murai

subfiles.about: The Japanese Embassy transmits biographical records for Commander Yatugi, Commander Taira, and Mr. Ishimura.
subfiles.summary: The Japanese Ambassador references Embassy note no. 95 of May 1, 1940 and transmits the biographical records of Commander Yatugi, Commander Taira, and Mr. Ishimura (Isimaru).
subfiles.title: Japanese Embassy Note No. 116 transmitting Biographical Records of Yatugi, Taira, and Ishimura

subfiles.about: The Japanese Embassy requests income tax exemptions for sixteen officials and employees representing Japan at the World's Fairs.
subfiles.summary: The Japanese Ambassador requests income tax exemptions for sixteen Japanese nationals dispatched in connection with the New York World's Fair and the San Francisco International Exposition. An attached list details their names, titles, and arrival details for the Japan Association for San Francisco and New York World Fairs, headed by Commissioner Rai Ishida, Clerk Toru Nagae, Manager Yoshio Yeto, and various temporary officials and employees.
subfiles.title: Japanese Embassy Note No. 117 requesting Tax Exemption for Exposition Personnel

subfiles.about: The State Department certifies the tax-exempt status of sixteen Japanese World's Fair and Exposition officials to the Treasury.
subfiles.summary: Secretary of State Cordell Hull transmits Japanese Embassy note no. 117 and its roster of exposition officials to Treasury Secretary Henry Morgenthau, Jr. Under Section 116(h) of the Internal Revenue Code, Hull certifies reciprocal tax exemption for the sixteen officials and employees sent to the United States for the New York and San Francisco expositions.
subfiles.title: State Department Letter to Secretary of the Treasury regarding World's Fair Personnel
subfiles.to: Henry Morgenthau, Jr., Secretary of the Treasury

subfiles.about: The State Department acknowledges the Japanese Embassy's tax exemption request for exposition personnel.
subfiles.summary: The Secretary of State acknowledges receipt of Japanese Embassy note no. 117 of May 21, 1940. The Ambassador is informed that copies of the note and list of exposition personnel have been transmitted to the competent authority of the United States Government with a view to granting the requested income tax exemptions.
subfiles.title: State Department Note to Japanese Ambassador acknowledging Note No. 117

subfiles.about: The Treasury Department confirms tax exemption instructions for naval inspector Moritoshi Maeda.
subfiles.summary: The Acting Secretary of the Treasury acknowledges the State Department's letter of May 16, 1940 regarding Mr. Moritoshi Maeda. In accordance with Section 116(h) of the Internal Revenue Code and the State Department's reciprocal certification, instructions will be issued to Internal Revenue officials.
subfiles.title: Treasury Department Letter regarding Tax Exemption for Moritoshi Maeda

subfiles.about: A State Department internal note urging that Japanese tax exemption requests not be granted without checking records.
subfiles.from: Assistant Secretary of State (Adolf A. Berle, Jr.)
subfiles.summary: An internal informal handwritten note addressing Assistant Secretary Adolf A. Berle, Jr. and the Division of Personnel regarding recent cases where tax exemption was granted without checking personnel records. The author asks for assistance in establishing a rule that exemptions will be refused until the appropriate biographical and background reports are received from the Japanese mission.
subfiles.title: State Department Internal Memorandum on Verifying Records Before Granting Tax Exemption
subfiles.to: Adolf A. Berle, Jr., Assistant Secretary of State

subfiles.about: The Treasury Department confirms tax exemption instructions for Kiyoshi Murai.
subfiles.summary: The Acting Secretary of the Treasury acknowledges the State Department's letter of May 21, 1940 concerning Mr. Kiyoshi Murai of the Japanese Government Raw Silk Conditioning House. Treasury confirms that appropriate instructions will be issued to Internal Revenue officials under Section 116(h) of the Internal Revenue Code.
subfiles.title: Treasury Department Letter regarding Tax Exemption for Kiyoshi Murai

subfiles.about: A cross-reference sheet regarding biographical data submitted for World's Fair Commissioner Kiyoshi Togasaki.
subfiles.summary: A cross-reference sheet indexing a Japanese Embassy communication dated May 21, 1940 (file 702.9411/567). The document records the submission of biographical data regarding Kiyoshi Togasaki, Commissioner to the New York World's Fair.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Sheet regarding Biographical Data of Kiyoshi Togasaki

subfiles.about: The Treasury Department confirms tax exemption instructions for personnel of the New York and San Francisco expositions.
subfiles.summary: The Acting Secretary of the Treasury acknowledges the State Department's letter of June 1, 1940 concerning the Japanese officials and employees representing Japan at the New York World's Fair and the San Francisco International Exposition. In view of the certification under Section 116(h) of the Internal Revenue Code, appropriate instructions will be issued to Internal Revenue officials.
subfiles.title: Treasury Department Letter regarding Tax Exemption for World's Fair and Exposition Personnel
